GTM AI enablement · architecture proposal
The Governed AI Harness
Local, user-level cost control for Claude Code — built from an LLM wiki, CLAUDE.md tiers, hooks, skills and a shared Databricks cache, shipped as one plugin.
Andy Hong
October 2026
Draft for team + leadership review
The problem
The gateway sees spend. It can't see intent.
Today
  • One company-wide AI gateway on Databricks enforces a hard budget cap
  • It meters tokens and calls, but not whether a call was worth making
  • Genie queries spend a second budget — warehouse and credits
  • Repeated Salesforce reporting questions are re-run from scratch
What that costs us
  • Premium models burned on trivial tasks
  • Tool calls that rediscover what we already know
  • No per-user forecast — we find the limit by hitting it
  • No team-level record that AI is used appropriately

Governed AI Harness · 03 · Delivered as one versioned Claude Code plugin
Why it matters
Cost scales with distinct, fresh questions — not with how often people ask
Predictable cost
Each skill is a unit with a known call and token budget; a task is the sum of its units
Fewer tool calls
Preloaded join logic and definitions replace round-trips that rediscover them
Better first-shot answers
The model reasons through our business rules from the first prompt
Provable governance
Every call logged with tier, cost and outcome — evidence for leadership
Governed AI Harness · 04
Architecture
End to end, two layers
Local harness runs on each laptop inside Claude Code. It knows the task, so it decides what is allowed and what is already answered.
Company layer is the Databricks AI gateway: OAuth, the hard cap, models, MCP tools, Genie and the shared cache.
Only two things cross the line: cache misses and calls the hooks allow.

Technical readout · predictable cost
A skill is a unit with a knowable budget
task cost = preload tokens + Σ (planned calls × cost per call) + output tokens
Wiki as planner
Preloaded markdown carries the plan: which calls fill which gaps, each mapped to a skill
Conditional calls
Gate each call: "only if node is missing or older than X" — most runs need zero
Estimate, then run
Show expected cost up front; confirm or refuse over threshold; flag unplanned calls

Data path
One query through the tiered cache
Best case: local hit — nothing touches the gateway.
Shared case: central hit with an unchanged source table — someone else already paid.
Worst case: one Genie run, written back so the next identical ask is cheap for everyone.

Governed AI Harness · 13
Data path · resolver
The resolver carries the most risk
A false miss costs one query. A false hit puts a wrong number in someone's report.
So: deterministic normalization first, semantic similarity only as a fallback — and parameters always match exactly.
When unsure, miss.
Governed AI Harness · 14
Technical readout · hardening the resolver
Five controls that make false hits nearly impossible
01
Normalize first
Canonical intent — time window, entity, filters, grouping — so most matching is exact structure
02
Bind parameters
Window, segment and filters match literally — never by similarity
03
Calibrate threshold
Label real query pairs; set the cutoff at zero false positives, then back off further
04
Test adversarially
Minimal pairs: same metric, different window; same window, different segment
05
Observe and reverse
Log every hit with signature and score; one-step "re-run fresh" for users

Package · the plugin
One install puts a teammate in the governed state
Governed AI Harness · 18 · Skill and agent names are proposed
Technical readout · install and lifecycle
Install, scaffold, distribute, upgrade
Bootstrap is idempotent
Detects existing CLAUDE.md files and merges, never clobbers. Creates root and project tiers, wiki folders and policy.yaml for users starting from zero.
Root vs project scope
Root holds posture and routing for every session. Each project declares its task types, tiers and which wiki subgraph to load.
Internal marketplace
A team git repo hosts the marketplace. Org-managed settings can pre-register it and pin the gateway so installs are consistent.
Versioned from day one
Semver on the plugin, a version key in policy.yaml, migrations for cache schema. Hooks stay backward compatible across one minor version.
Governed AI Harness · 19
Assessment
Strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats
Strengths
  • Governance as code — versioned and reviewable
  • Shapes behavior before the gateway
  • Wiki is a productivity and a cost lever
Weaknesses
  • CLAUDE.md alone is advisory
  • Stale wiki content is confidently wrong
  • Hooks and cache are new upkeep
Opportunities
  • Plugin becomes the GTM-wide standard
  • Proven cache promotes to the gateway
  • Telemetry gives leadership showback
Threats
  • Preload bloat can outspend saved calls
  • Teams fork CLAUDE.md and drift
  • False blocks get the harness disabled
Governed AI Harness · 20
Adoption
Two blast radii, two different games
OUR TEAM · THE PLUGIN
Make the governed path the easy path
  • Lead with better answers, not limits
  • Cost control is a byproduct people don't manage
  • Value first, enforcement earned with evidence
  • Small, high-trust group: fast feedback
COMPANY · THE GATEWAY
Infrastructure, not adoption
  • Nobody adopts a hard cap — they hit it
  • The harness keeps us far from that floor
  • We complement it; we don't duplicate it
  • Promotion needs data the pilot produces

Governed AI Harness · 23
Risks and mitigations
What could go wrong, and the control for each
Risk
Mitigation
Shared cache leaks across permissions
access_scope in the key; restricted data keyed per user or excluded
Stale or wrong wiki content
Named owners per domain, provenance tags, staleness flags
False cache hits
Precision-first resolver, exact params, logged hits, re-run button
Preload bloat
Scoped subgraphs; track input tokens per session
Harness gets disabled
Warn mode first; block only with evidence; fast override path
Genie billing assumption wrong
Confirm credit model with the Databricks billing owner first
